newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures dip on pre-Iraq news selling.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures dip on pre-Iraq news selling.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures edged lower in low volume on Friday as some players expecting some word from the U.N. about Iraqi oil exports liquidated long positions ahead of the weekend .
By 1010 GMT September Brent was down eight cents at $18.36 a barrel, with gas oil 50 cents lower at $164.75 a tonne.
"It looks like players are liquidating longs ahead of the weekend," one broker said. "Whatever Iraq news comes out over the weekend, it should drive the market lower."

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan is expected to meet U.N. officals this weekend to discuss a food distribution plan submitted by Iraq on Monday. The U.N. has said the review was expected to be completed by the end of July.
"The market sentiment seems to reflect a reluctance to go into the weekend long because of the Iraqi influence," GNI Research said in a report.
Nymex September crude futures trading on ACCESS were last done at $19.65, 12 cents below the pit trade settle at $19.77 after NYMEX crude firmed 10 cents on the back of a rally in August gasoline.
Iraqi oil sales under a U.N. oil-for-food deal have been delayed while the U.N. considers Baghdad's aid distribution plan.

The $2 billion six-month deal which came into effect on June 8 has been split into two three-month, $1 billion tranches and members of the U.N. sanctions committee said on Thursday Baghdad would not be allowed to change deadlines for the first tranche.
Baghdad will also not be allowed to carry over more than five percent of its oil allocation from the first tranche into the second, the U.N. has said.

Industry analysts suggest this means Iraq will have to squeeze out 1.5-2 million barrels per day when exports resume, possibly in mid-August, in order to meet its $1 billion cash target by early September.
